nodes.summary: For every requested arity $r \in \mathbb{N}$ and every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the $d$-ary min-heap built from $xs$ with requested arity $r$ has arity equal to the normalized arity of $r$, namely $\max(2, r)$.
nodes.title: Arity of a $d$-ary heap built from a list

nodes.summary: For every $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type, the number of elements of $h$, counted with multiplicity, equals the length of its backing array.
nodes.title: Size of a $d$-ary min-heap

nodes.summary: For every $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type and all values $x \ne y$, the multiplicity of $y$ among the elements of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $h$ equals the multiplicity of $y$ among the elements of $h$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a $d$-ary heap preserves other multiplicities

nodes.summary: For every $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type and every value $x$, the multiplicity of $x$ among the elements of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $h$ is one more than its multiplicity among the elements of $h$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a $d$-ary heap raises the multiplicity by one

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$, $i$ and $k$, the child of index $i$ with zero-based offset $k$ in a contiguous level-order $d$-ary tree is the index $d i + k + 1$.
nodes.title: Child index in a $d$-ary heap array

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number and $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ an array with entries in a type carrying a relation $\le$. The array $a$ is $d$-ary heap ordered when $d \ge 2$ and every nonroot entry is at least the entry at its parent index: $a_{\lfloor (i-1)/d \rfloor} \le a_i$ for every index $i$ with $0 < i < n$.
nodes.title: $d$-ary heap order

nodes.summary: A $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ consists of a natural number $d \ge 2$, its arity, and an array $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ of elements of $\alpha$, stored in level order, that is $d$-ary heap ordered: $a_{\lfloor (i-1)/d \rfloor} \le a_i$ for every index $i$ with $0 < i < n$.
nodes.title: $d$-ary min-heap

nodes.summary: For every nonempty array $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of entries of the array obtained from $a$ by the last-to-root move equals the multiset of entries of $a$ with one occurrence of $a_0$ removed.
nodes.title: Last-to-root move in a $d$-ary heap removes one copy of the root

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $a$ be a $d$-ary heap ordered array with at least two entries over a linearly ordered type, and let $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{m-1})$ be the array obtained from $a$ by the last-to-root move. Then $b$ is ready for a $d$-ary sift-down at index $0$: $d \ge 2$, $0 < m$, and $b_{\lfloor (j-1)/d \rfloor} \le b_j$ for every index $j$ with $0 < j < m$ whose parent index $\lfloor (j-1)/d \rfloor$…
nodes.title: Last-to-root move in a $d$-ary heap is ready for sift-down

nodes.summary: For a nonempty array $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{n-1})$, the last-to-root move swaps $a_0$ and $a_{n-1}$ and then deletes the last entry, producing an array $b = (b_0, \dots, b_{n-2})$ of length $n - 1$: when $n \ge 2$, $b_0 = a_{n-1}$ and $b_i = a_i$ for $0 < i < n - 1$, and $b$ is empty when $n = 1$.
nodes.title: Last-to-root move on an array

nodes.summary: Let $d$, $i$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$ and $k < d$. Then the $d$-ary parent of the child of $i$ with zero-based offset $k$, that is, of the index $di + k + 1$, is $i$.
nodes.title: The parent of a $d$-ary child

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$ be a natural number, let $a$ be an array over any type, write $|a|$ for its size, and let $i$ be an index with $0 < i < |a|$. Then the $d$-ary parent of $i$ is also less than $|a|$.
nodes.title: The $d$-ary parent of a valid index is valid

nodes.summary: Let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$ and $i > 0$. Then the $d$-ary parent of $i$ is strictly less than $i$.
nodes.title: A $d$-ary parent has a smaller index

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $d$ and $i$, the $d$-ary parent of $i$ is $\lfloor (i - 1)/d \rfloor$, computed in the natural numbers: $i - 1$ is truncated at $0$, so the parent of $0$ is $0$, and division by $0$ gives $0$.
nodes.title: Parent index in a $d$-ary tree

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $d \ge 2$, and let $a$ be an array over $\alpha$ that is $d$-ary heap ordered, with size $|a|$. Then for every $x \in \alpha$, the array obtained by appending $x$ to $a$ is ready for $d$-ary sifting up at index $|a|$, the position of $x$; in particular every nonroot entry other than $x$ is at least its $d$-ary parent.
nodes.title: Pushing onto a $d$-ary heap leaves it ready for sifting up

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $a$ be an array over $\alpha$, and let $i$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$. The array produced by $d$-ary sifting down from index $i$ in $a$ has the same multiset of entries as $a$.
nodes.title: Sifting down in a $d$-ary heap preserves the multiset of entries

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $d \ge 2$, and let $a$ be an array over $\alpha$ that is ready for $d$-ary sifting down at an index $i$. Then the array produced by $d$-ary sifting down from index $i$ in $a$ is $d$-ary heap ordered.
nodes.title: Sifting down restores $d$-ary heap order

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $a$ be an array over $\alpha$, and let $i$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$. The array produced by $d$-ary sifting down from index $i$ in $a$ is a permutation of $a$.
nodes.title: Sifting down in a $d$-ary heap permutes the array

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array over a type with a relation $\le$, and let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers. Write $|a|$ for the size of $a$ and $p(j)$ for the $d$-ary parent of an index $j$. The array $a$ is ready for $d$-ary sifting down at $i$ when $d \ge 2$, $i < |a|$, every index $j$ with $0 < j < |a|$ and $p(j) \ne i$ satisfies $a_{p(j)} \le a_j$, and, if $i > 0$, every index $j$ with $0 < j < |a|$ and $p(j) = i$ satisfies…
nodes.title: Readiness for $d$-ary sift-down

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $a$ be an array over $\alpha$, and let $i$ and $d$ be natural numbers with $d \ge 2$. Sifting down from $i$ in $a$ returns $a$ if $i$ has no valid $d$-ary child in $a$. Otherwise let $c$ be the smallest valid $d$-ary child of $i$, with ties broken toward the lowest child offset: if $a_c < a_i$, swap the entries at $i$ and $c$ and sift down from $c$ in the resulting…
nodes.title: $d$-ary sift-down

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type and let $i$ be a natural number. The array obtained from $a$ by $d$-ary sift-up from index $i$ has the same multiset of entries as $a$.
nodes.title: Sifting up preserves the multiset of entries

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, of length $|a|$ with entries $a_0, \dots, a_{|a|-1}$, let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers, and write $p(j) = \lfloor (j-1)/d \rfloor$ for the parent of an index $j > 0$. Suppose $a$ is ready for sift-up at $i$: $d \ge 2$, $i < |a|$, $a_{p(j)} \le a_j$ for every $0 < j < |a|$ with $j \ne i$, and, if $i > 0$, $a_{p(i)} \le a_j$ for every $0 < j < |a|$ with $p(j) = i$.…
nodes.title: Sift-up restores $d$-ary heap order

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type and let $i$ be a natural number. The array obtained from $a$ by $d$-ary sift-up from index $i$ is a permutation of $a$.
nodes.title: Sifting up permutes the array

nodes.summary: Let $a = (a_0, \dots, a_{|a|-1})$ be an array over a type with a relation $\le$, let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers, and write $p(j) = \lfloor (j-1)/d \rfloor$ for the parent of an index $j > 0$. The array $a$ is ready for sift-up at $i$ when $d \ge 2$, $i < |a|$, $a_{p(j)} \le a_j$ for every $0 < j < |a|$ with $j \ne i$, and, if $i > 0$, $a_{p(i)} \le a_j$ for every $0 < j < |a|$ with $p(j) = i$.
nodes.title: Arrays ready for $d$-ary sift-up

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, of length $|a|$ with entries $a_0, \dots, a_{|a|-1}$, let $i$ be a natural number, and write $p(i) = \lfloor (i-1)/d \rfloor$ for the parent of $i > 0$. The sift-up of $a$ from $i$ is defined recursively: if $0 < i < |a|$ and $a_i < a_{p(i)}$, it is the sift-up from $p(i)$ of the array obtained from $a$ by swapping the entries at positions $i$ and…
nodes.title: $d$-ary sift-up

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type, of length $|a|$, let $d$, $i$ and $s$ be natural numbers, and call $d i + k + 1$ the child of $i$ at offset $k$. Scanning the offsets $s, s + 1, \dots, d - 1$, this returns the index of a scanned child of $i$ below $|a|$ whose entry in $a$ is least among those, taking the smallest offset among ties, or nothing if no scanned child index is below $|a|$.
nodes.title: Smallest child among the offsets from $s$

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 2$, let $a$ be an array over a linearly ordered type and let $i$ and $c$ be natural numbers. If the smallest valid child of $i$ in the $d$-ary heap array $a$ is $c$, then $i < c$.
nodes.title: The smallest child lies after its parent

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array of length $|a|$ over a linearly ordered type and let $d$, $i$ and $c$ be natural numbers. If the smallest valid child of $i$ in the $d$-ary heap array $a$ is $c$, then $c < |a|$.
nodes.title: The smallest child is a valid index

nodes.summary: Let $a$ be an array of length $|a|$ over a linearly ordered type and let $d$ and $i$ be natural numbers. The children of $i$ are the indices $d i + k + 1$ for $0 \le k < d$, and a child is valid when it is below $|a|$. The smallest child of $i$ is the valid child of $i$ with the least entry, taking the smallest offset $k$ among ties, or nothing if $i$ has no valid child.
nodes.title: Smallest child in a $d$-ary heap array

nodes.summary: For every requested arity $r$ and every list $xs$ over a linearly ordered type, the multiset of elements of the min-heap of arity $\max(2, r)$ built from $xs$ by successive insertions equals the multiset of entries of $xs$.
nodes.title: Building a heap from a list keeps its elements

nodes.summary: For a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type and a value $x$, the multiset of elements of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $h$ is the multiset of elements of $h$ with one more occurrence of $x$.
nodes.title: Insertion into a d-ary heap adds one occurrence

nodes.summary: The multiset of elements of a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type is the multiset of the entries of its level-order storage array, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Elements of a d-ary heap

nodes.summary: For a natural number $r$ (the requested arity), the empty heap is the $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type with arity $d = \max(2, r)$ and an empty storage array; a requested arity below two is thus normalized to two.
nodes.title: Empty d-ary heap

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then $h'$ has the same arity as $h$.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum preserves the arity of a d-ary heap

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then the multiset of elements of $h$ is the multiset of elements of $h'$ with one more occurrence of $x$.
nodes.title: Extracted minimum and remaining d-ary heap recover the original elements

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then the multiplicity of $x$ in the multiset of elements of $h'$ is its multiplicity in the multiset of elements of $h$ minus one.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum of a d-ary heap lowers its multiplicity by one

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then the multiset of elements of $h'$ is obtained from the multiset of elements of $h$ by removing one occurrence of $x$.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum of a d-ary heap removes one occurrence

nodes.summary: For a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ over a linearly ordered type, extracting the minimum from $h$ returns no result if and only if the storage array of $h$ is empty.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum of a d-ary heap fails exactly on the empty heap

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then $x \le y$ for every element $y$ of the multiset of elements of $h$.
nodes.title: The extracted minimum of a d-ary heap is a lower bound

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap over a linearly ordered type. If extracting the minimum from $h$ succeeds, returning a value $x$ and a heap $h'$, then $x$ belongs to the multiset of elements of $h$.
nodes.title: The extracted minimum of a d-ary heap is one of its elements

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap. If extracting the minimum of $h$ returns a value $x$ and a heap $h'$ of arity $d'$, then $d' \ge 2$ and the storage array $a$ of $h'$ is heap-ordered: for every index $i$ with $0 < i < |a|$, the entry $a_{\lfloor (i-1)/d' \rfloor}$ is at most $a_i$.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum leaves a heap-ordered $d$-ary heap

nodes.summary: For a $d$-ary min-heap $h$, extracting the minimum returns nothing if the storage array of $h$ is empty. Otherwise it returns the root entry (the entry at index $0$) together with the heap obtained from $h$ by removing its root: the last entry moves to the root and sifts down along a single $d$-ary child path.
nodes.title: Extracting the minimum of a $d$-ary min-heap

nodes.summary: For a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ with nonempty storage array, the heap obtained from $h$ by removing its root has the same arity $d$ as $h$.
nodes.title: Removing the root of a $d$-ary heap preserves its arity

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap whose storage array $a$ is nonempty. Removing the root of $h$ gives the heap of arity $d$ whose storage array is empty if $a$ has one entry. Otherwise the last entry of $a$ replaces the root, the last position is dropped, and the new root is repeatedly swapped with its smallest $d$-ary child while that child is smaller.
nodes.title: Removing the root of a $d$-ary min-heap

nodes.summary: For a $d$-ary min-heap $h$, the minimum query on $h$ (which returns the entry at index $0$ of the storage array, if any) returns nothing if and only if the storage array of $h$ is empty.
nodes.title: The minimum query on a $d$-ary heap fails exactly when it is empty

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap. If the minimum query on $h$ returns $x$, then $x \le y$ for every element $y$ of the multiset of elements of $h$.
nodes.title: The minimum query on a $d$-ary heap returns a least element

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap. If the minimum query on $h$ returns $x$, then $x$ belongs to the multiset of elements of $h$.
nodes.title: The minimum query on a $d$-ary heap returns an element of the heap

nodes.summary: The minimum query on a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ returns the entry at index $0$ (the root) of the storage array of $h$, or nothing if the array is empty.
nodes.title: Minimum query on a $d$-ary min-heap

nodes.summary: For every natural number $d \ge 2$, the normalized arity $\max(2, d)$ of $d$ equals $d$.
nodes.title: Normalization leaves a valid arity unchanged

nodes.summary: For every natural number $r$, the normalized arity $\max(2, r)$ of $r$ is at least $2$.
nodes.title: Normalized arities are at least two

nodes.summary: The normalized arity of a requested arity $r \in \mathbb{N}$ is $\max(2, r)$: the requested arities $0$ and $1$ become $2$ (the binary-heap policy), and every $r \ge 2$ is left unchanged.
nodes.title: Normalized heap arity

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $r \in \mathbb{N}$ be a requested arity, and let $d = \max(2, r)$. The min-heap built from the empty list is the empty min-heap of arity $d$, and the min-heap built from a list with head $x$ and tail $xs$ of elements of $\alpha$ is obtained by inserting $x$ into the min-heap built from $xs$. Thus the min-heap built from $[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ starts from the empty min-heap…
nodes.title: Building a $d$-ary min-heap from a list

nodes.summary: Let $h$ be a $d$-ary min-heap of arity $d$ and let $x$ be a value. Then the level-order array of the heap obtained by inserting $x$ into $h$ is $d$-ary heap-ordered for the same arity $d$.
nodes.title: Insertion keeps a $d$-ary heap ordered

nodes.summary: Inserting a value $x$ into a $d$-ary min-heap $h$ of arity $d$ gives the heap of the same arity $d$ whose array is obtained by appending $x$ at the end of the level-order array of $h$ and sifting it up from that last index: while the current index $i > 0$ holds an entry strictly smaller than the entry at its parent index $\lfloor (i-1)/d \rfloor$, the two entries are swapped and the process continues from the…
nodes.title: Insertion into a $d$-ary heap

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type, let $d \ge 2$, and let $a$ be an array of elements of $\alpha$ that is $d$-ary heap-ordered. Then $a_0 \le a_i$ for every index $i$ smaller than the size of $a$.
nodes.title: The root of a $d$-ary heap-ordered array is a minimum

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
